robot: Unitree G1 humanoid, 29 joints (legs 12, waist 3, arms 7 + 7), 1.32 m; Unitree's walking policy and a running policy built in; fist pads on both wrists

frame.suite: heading only: the yaw of the pelvis IMU in the venue's world frame; the robot senses no position, so x and y stay 0
frame.base_text: the robot base frame: on the floor under the pelvis, +X the way the pelvis faces at the start of the call, +Y left, +Z up (only the heading is sensed, from the pelvis IMU)

torso.note: the waist (yaw, roll, pitch), joint targets through the stand type

left.note: 7 joints: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist roll, pitch, yaw; joint targets through the stand type

right.note: 7 joints: shoulder pitch, roll, yaw, elbow, wrist roll, pitch, yaw; joint targets through the stand type

legs.note: 12 joints (left hip pitch, roll, yaw, knee, ankle pitch, roll; then the right leg's) through the joints type: the default gains, nothing balances the robot

locomotion.note: Unitree's G1 walking policy (`walk` rows at 50 Hz; the waist and arms keep their targets): at the largest forward command (0.8) it walks about 0.6 m/s; it follows with lag and barely moves in its first second; at zero command it marks time on the spot and drifts a centimetre or two per second; moving the arms disturbs it. Coming from another mode it first blends the legs to its stance (0.3 s) and holds still until steady (up to 2 s). Each call ends with 1 s of zero command. The running policy and two more walkers are native action types (run, run_arms, walk_falcon, walk_agile).

resets.note: Embodied Olympics allows 5 resets (describe_robot: resets): each starts a new attempt from the same start; only the last attempt is graded, and a success ends the run.

notes: Joint targets are absolute angles (rad); a target moves at most the joint's speed limit per 10 ms step. The arms (left, right) and the waist (torso part) take joint targets through the `stand` action type: the platform holds the legs in the standing stance with stiff gains and gravity support but no balance feedback, so a fast or hard arm swing can tip the robot over; a move_robot call on these parts switches the legs back to `stand`. The legs part uses the `joints` type (every joint at the default gains; nothing balances the robot in that mode). Legs and arm goals use different action types: send them in separate move_robot calls, or send rows of any of the robot's action types with execute_trajectory space native (stand, walk, run, run_arms, joints, lowcmd, walk_falcon, walk_agile; layouts and bounds in describe_robot). move_robot and joint rows for the arms and the waist (torso part) start from the last `stand` row sent through these tools (at the start of an attempt: the start command), grips included; locomote and the legs part start from the joint targets in force and keep a grip closed while that hand holds something (holding_* in proprio_now), open otherwise. On a fist pad a grip of 0.5 or more closes it (it holds a grippable object within 3.5 cm of the palm). From walk_falcon or walk_agile, give `walk` a zero command for about 2 s before `stand` (straight to `stand` usually ends in a fall); locomote ends each call with 1 s of zero command. Between calls the robot is frozen: time passes only inside calls. There is no end-effector pose command: describe_robot's spec_file (robot_facts) has each joint's range, speed and torque limits, default gains and the stance. The robot senses no position: the state shows its heading (the pelvis IMU's yaw) only, and locomote's displacement reports the turn (dyaw), while dx and dy stay 0: judge distances from the cameras. Once an attempt is over, results carry the referee's call (outcome, stages_reached of stages_total).

patch.notes: Joint targets are absolute angles (rad); a target moves at most the joint's speed limit per 10 ms step. On the beam every part (legs, torso = the waist, arms) takes joint targets through the `joints` type at the default gains, the way the robot starts (held by a `lowcmd` row of those targets); nothing balances the robot but your own targets. A `stand` row moves the legs to the normal stance and a `walk` row starts the normal gait: both put the feet beside the beam, so locomote is not offered here. move_robot and joint rows start from the last `joints` row sent through these tools (at the start of an attempt: the start targets); other gains, velocities and feed-forward torques are the native `lowcmd` type (execute_trajectory space native; layouts and bounds of every type (stand, walk, run, run_arms, joints, lowcmd, walk_falcon, walk_agile) in describe_robot). Between calls the robot is frozen: time passes only inside calls. There is no end-effector pose command: describe_robot's spec_file (robot_facts) has each joint's range, speed and torque limits, default gains and the stance. The robot senses no position: the state shows its heading (the pelvis IMU's yaw) only, and locomote's displacement reports the turn (dyaw), while dx and dy stay 0: judge distances from the cameras. Once an attempt is over, results carry the referee's call (outcome, stages_reached of stages_total).

Joint targets are absolute angles (rad); a target moves at most the joint's speed limit per 10 ms step. Here every part (legs, torso = the waist, arms) takes joint targets through the `joints` type at the default gains (`stand` keeps the legs in the stance with a feed-forward meant for standing on the ground); nothing else holds the body. The bar is not a free body: the holding_* flags stay 0 on it. move_robot and joint rows start from the last `joints` row sent through these tools (at the start of an attempt: the start targets and grips), so a goal without a gripper keeps the last grip sent here; after native rows, give `gripper` in the next goals. A grip is the hand's closure command (0 open, 1 closed; a full close takes about 0.1 s). Other gains, velocities and feed-forward torques are the native `lowcmd` type (execute_trajectory space native; layouts and bounds of every type (stand, walk, run, run_arms, joints, lowcmd, walk_falcon, walk_agile) in describe_robot). locomote is not offered here. Between calls the robot is frozen: time passes only inside calls. There is no end-effector pose command: describe_robot's spec_file (robot_facts) has each joint's range, speed and torque limits, default gains and the stance. The robot senses no position: the state shows its heading (the pelvis IMU's yaw) only, and locomote's displacement reports the turn (dyaw), while dx and dy stay 0: judge distances from the cameras. Once an attempt is over, results carry the referee's call (outcome, stages_reached of stages_total).

locomotion.note: The running policy (`run` rows at 50 Hz; it drives all 29 joints and swings the arms): vx from 0 to about 4 m/s (it falls above that), |vy| up to 0.12, |wz| up to 0.5. The command changes at most 1.5 m/s per second, so a call's closing zero command only starts the slowing: from 2.4 m/s stopping takes about 2 s and 2.3 m. Switching to stand, walk or joints above about 0.6 m/s usually ends in a fall. Unitree's walking policy is the native `walk` type.
